decisionMemo.businessProblem: A busy clinic has long appointment waits AND a genuine follow-up problem; the owner is unsure which to fix first.

rootCauseDiagnosis.description: Operational bottleneck limiting speed of service delivery
rootCauseDiagnosis.mechanismDescription: High turnaround time prevents customers from using service frequently, driving them to alternatives. Bottleneck creates queue, which increases errors and complaints.
alternativeExplanations: Pricing may be too high relative to speed
Marketing may not communicate speed differentiation
missingEvidenceFor: Root cause of turnaround delay (equipment vs labor vs process)
Customer awareness of speed-to-market from competitors

criticalConstraints.description: No customer relationship management system or loyalty program infrastructure

intervention.title: Implement waitlist system to manage demand
intervention.objective: Reduce customer frustration by setting expectations and freeing capacity for retention
intervention.rationale: While turnaround time remains high, a waitlist prevents customer abandonment
intervention.whyThisNow: Immediate relief for customer experience while longer-term capacity fix is designed

steps.title: Design waitlist communication template
steps.description: Create customer communication explaining wait time and providing estimated completion date
steps.successCriteria: Template tested with 3 customers, feedback incorporated

steps.title: Implement waitlist tracking system
steps.description: Use spreadsheet or simple tool to track order position and manage customer expectations
steps.successCriteria: All customer orders tracked, completion estimates accurate within 10%

steps.title: Monitor customer satisfaction weekly
steps.description: Collect feedback on waitlist experience via follow-up call or survey
steps.successCriteria: Satisfaction score improves to 7+/10, repeat customer inquiry rate increases

failureRisks: Customers may still defect to competitors even with better communication
Waitlist may discourage new customer acquisition
intervention.fallbackPlan: Remove waitlist and implement expedited service tier at premium pricing

intervention.title: Diagnose turnaround time bottleneck
intervention.objective: Identify specific cause of high turnaround (equipment, labor, process) to guide intervention
intervention.rationale: Without diagnosis, capacity solution will be misaligned and costly
intervention.whyThisNow: Prerequisite for any structural capacity improvement. Can run in parallel with Containment

steps.title: Time study: Map current process end-to-end
steps.description: Observe and document each step in the service delivery process with time stamps
steps.successCriteria: Process map complete, bottleneck identified (where time accumulates)

steps.title: Interview operations team on constraints
steps.description: Ask what limits speed at each step: equipment capacity, labor availability, process design
steps.successCriteria: Team consensus on 1-2 primary constraints preventing speed

steps.title: Create capability roadmap
steps.description: Design solution (equipment upgrade, process redesign, staffing, or hybrid)
steps.successCriteria: Roadmap costed and sequenced, board/owner approval obtained

successMetrics: Capacity improvement solution designed and costed
failureRisks: Multiple bottlenecks discovered requiring simultaneous fixes
intervention.fallbackPlan: Prioritize highest-ROI bottleneck only, phase other fixes over 6 months

factors.rationale: Expected revenue impact: SIGNIFICANT. Urgency: HIGH
Duration: 8 days. Team capacity: MEDIUM. Cost: LOW
Failure risks: 2. Fallback plan available: Yes
Cost band: LOW vs Expected impact: SIGNIFICANT

recommendedInterventions.sequencingReason: Quick implementation builds momentum and shows progress

intervention.title: Implement capacity improvement solution
intervention.objective: Increase service delivery speed to competitive range (diagnosis dependent)
intervention.rationale: Removing the turnaround bottleneck unlocks customer retention and revenue growth
intervention.whyThisNow: After root cause is diagnosed and solution is designed. May require capital approval

steps.title: Secure capital and/or budget approval
steps.description: Present business case to board or lender for investment in capacity solution

steps.title: Execute equipment upgrade or process redesign
steps.description: Based on diagnosis, implement the designed solution (procurement, install, training)
steps.successCriteria: New equipment operational or new process in place and tested

steps.title: Verify turnaround time improvement
steps.description: Measure actual turnaround on 20 consecutive orders vs baseline
steps.successCriteria: Turnaround time reduced to target (e.g., 50% reduction), consistency verified

failureRisks: New capacity utilization is lower than projected
Quality issues emerge with new process
intervention.fallbackPlan: Revert to manual process, hire temp labor to increase capacity, revisit capital investment in 6 months

scenarios.name: Aggressive Recovery (Best Case)
scenarios.description: Execute all interventions in optimal sequence with full team commitment
assumptions: Team capacity fully available (no other initiatives)
Client budget approved for all recommended interventions
No external market shocks during implementation
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Revenue recovery within 90 days, competitive positioning restored
risks: Cascading failures if one intervention stumbles

scenarios.name: Staged Implementation (Recommended)
scenarios.description: Execute top 3 prioritized interventions sequentially, measure, then decide on next wave
assumptions: Top 3 interventions address critical path to revenue recovery
Team capacity for 1-2 major initiatives at a time
Monthly review gates to assess progress and adjust
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Measurable improvement in 60 days, foundation for growth set
risks: Slower overall recovery than aggressive path
Competitors may advance while we execute gradually

scenarios.name: Defensive Hold (Minimal Risk)
scenarios.description: Execute containment interventions only to stabilize immediate crisis
assumptions: Focus on preserving cash and customer base
External investment or M&A may be needed for growth
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Stabilize revenue decline, buy time for external support
risks: Does not address root causes; temporary relief only
Competitors gain market share during hold period
Team morale declines with no visible improvement
